DICTATED IN OPEN COURT Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Criminal Appeal No.1774/2020 and M.Cr.C No.33573/2020 are filed being aggrieved of judgment dated 22.11.2019 passed by learned Vth Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal in Sessions Trial No.197/2019 acquitting the accused persons, namely, Mohammad Tarik (husband of deceased NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:16389 2 CRA-1774-2020 Rimsha), Mohammad Laeek (father-in-law of deceased Rimsha), Seema (mother-in-law of deceased Rimsha) and Jainab @ Aman Ali (brother-in-law of deceased Rimsha) from the charges under Sections 498A and 304B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "I.P.C") and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

sentences.text: Ms.Smita Varma, learned counsel for the complainant submits that the marriage of Rimsha (since deceased) was performed with Tarik on 2.1.2017 and Rimsha died on 18.8.2018 i.e. within less than seven years of her marriage with Tarik and, therefore, presumption under Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 is to be drawn against the accused persons and the onus was on the accused persons to prove their case.
The learned Trial Court has recorded a finding of acquittal on the basis of the testimony of the prosecution witnesses, which is contrary to the provisions of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

Hence, the finding of acquittal recorded by the learned Trial Court be reversed and the finding of conviction be recorded against the accused persons.
3

Shri Arvind Singh, learned Government Advocate for the State opposes the impugned judgment of acquittal and submits that even the State has filed M.Cr.C No.33573/2020 assailing the impugned judgment of acquittal and prays for reversal of the finding of acquittal recorded by the learned Trial Court.
4 We have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the record.
5 It is an admitted fact that marriage of Rimsha with Tarik was performed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16389 3 CRA-1774-2020 on 2.1.2017 and Rimsha committed suicide on 18.8.2018.
6 Naib Tahsildar Dinesh Kumar Uikey (PW.9) states that he had carried out proceedings for preparation of Shav Panchnama on 19.8.2018.

He categorically states that none of the witnesses,
namely, Sadma Ali (PW.1), Irshad Ali (PW.2), Mohammad Anad Khan (PW.4) and Syed Daud Ali (PW.5) had informed him at any point of time that Rimsha committed suicide for demand of dowry.
7 Sadma Ali (PW.1) in Paragraph No.24 of her testimony states that Laeek Miyan had performed marriage with Seema three and half months prior to the death of Rimsha.
She admits that Jainab had very cordial relations with Rimsha.

This witness admits that she was unaware of any dispute having taken place between Jainab and Rimsha and then she states that in the month of April, a dispute had taken place and in her case diary statement, she had not made any mention about the said dispute.

This witness in Paragraph No.25 admits that her daughter was pregnant and that time,
she was suffering from low blood pressure and Jainab used to hide food but this witness had not mentioned this fact in her case diary statement.

She admits that Jainab used to taunt Rimsha that she remained unveiled in the open premises and if this thing is not mentioned in the case diary statement then she cannot give any reason for the same.
8 Sadma Ali (PW.1) in Paragraph No.26 admits that the delivery of Rimsha had taken place at Central Hospital, Bhopal.
The hospital bill of about Rs.20,000/- was paid by Tarik @ Shahrukh.
Later on, this witness improvises her version stating that Rs.20,000/-was taken by Tarik from her.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16389 4 CRA-1774-2020
In Paragraph No.26, this witness admits contradiction in her case diary statement.

There is another contradiction that on one hand, it is stated that Jainab used to hide food to torture Rimsha and on the other hand, this witness admits that there was no dispute between Rimsha and Jainab.
This witness also admits that Rimsha during her pregnancy resided at her parental home for a period of seven months.

sentences.text: Irshad Ali (PW.2) admits in Paragraph No.35 of his cross-examination admits that there were several contradictions in his case diary statement.
This witness admits that Jainab used to accuse Rimsha of having affair with other boys but this fact was not narrated by him in his case diary statement.
10 Samina (PW.3) states that the accused Seema used to ask Rimsha to carry out household work and there used to be dispute between Seema and Rimsha on such issues.
In Paragraph Nos.17 & 28, this witness admits contradictions in her case diary statement with regard to accusation against Jainab and Seema.

Another contradiction in the testimony of Samina (PW.3)
is that she had mentioned that one and a quarter months after the delivery, the accused persons used to compel Rimsha to fill Cooler with a Bucket whereas it is alleged that after two months of delivery, Rimsha had started residing at her parental home.
The aforesaid inconsistency casts serious doubt on the veracity of the said allegation.

11 Ms.Smita Varma, learned counsel for the complainant has though contended that the accused persons had killed the deceased and that the family members were not allowed to meet and see the dead body of Rimsha but that contention is contrary to the testimony of Irshad Ali (PW.2), who NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:16389 5 CRA-1774-2020 admits that they had received a phone call about the deceased Rimsha being admitted in the hospital and at hospital, he had met his ''Sadu'' and ''Sali''.
12 Naib Tahsildar Dinesh Kumar Uikey (PW.9) admits that the Shav Panchnama was prepared in front of the complainant party.

Sadma Ali (PW.1) states that she had not seen the dead body of Rimsha till the postmortem was conducted whereas Samina (PW.3) states that she had seen the dead body of Rimsha in Emergency Ward of Hamidiya Hospital.
She alleges that there were injury marks on the body of Rimsha but that assertion is contrary to the testimony of the postmortem doctor.
13 Irshad Ali (PW.2) admits that Tarik had never demanded any money from him.

Irshad Ali (PW.2) admits that the major cause of dispute was that Tarik was not willing to leave Rimsha in her parental home and he used to bring her to her parental home 2-3 times in a month and used to take her back with him.
Irshad Ali (PW.2) admits that he had solemnized marriage of his two daughters simultaneously and there was no demand of dowry at the time of their marriage.

There is general and omnibus allegation with regard to demand of Rs.5,00,000/- for the purpose of laying roof of the house of Tarik but that has not been substantiated through any independent evidence.
14 Mohammad Anad Khan (PW.4) in Paragraph No.14 of his cross- examination admits that while giving his case diary statement (Exhibit P/6), he had not informed the police with regard to any dispute.
He admits that after 5-6 months of marriage, altercation had taken place, was not narrated by him in his case diary statement.
There are other contradictions in his case diary statement.

Mohammad Anad Khan (PW.4) admits in Paragraph No.25 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:16389 6 CRA-1774-2020 that he cannot specify the date, month, or year on which any money was allegedly demanded for laying roof.

15 Syed Daud Ali (PW.5) in Paragraph No.23 states that in Exhibit D/2, if it is not mentioned that Laeek had demanded Rs.5,00,000/- for laying roof and then he cannot give any explanation for the same.
16 Faizan (PW.6) admits that at the time of recording of his case diary statement (Exhibit D/3), he did not inform the police that Laeek had demanded Rs.5,00,000/- for laying roof.
17 When all the foregoing facts are taken into consideration then it is evident that the death of Rimsha occurred as a result of suicide.
It is indeed unfortunate that a young woman took her own life within less than two years of her marriage

, however, none of the prosecution witnesses have The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Mohd. Tarik on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38212429/
3 been able to substantiate either a demand for dowry or cruelty connected with such a demand.

sentences.text:
Infact, Sadma Ali (PW.1) admits that on 18.7.2018, the entire family had gone on a picnic with Tarik,
during which they shared a happy and harmonious time.
Thus, it is evident that onus was on the prosecution to have proved demand of dowry and associated cruelty immediately preceding the death of Rimsha.

18 The law in this regard is crystal clear as has been laid down by the Apex Court in Jagjit Singh versus State of Punjab (2018) 10 SCC 593 wherein it is held that unless and until it is proved that cruelty was meted out or demand of dowry was raised soon before the death, no presumption can be drawn that the death occurred as a result of dowry harassment or cruelty associated therewith.

In our considered opinion,
learned Trial Court has rightly recorded the finding of acquittal vide impugned judgment dated 22.11.2019 passed by learned Vth Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal in Sessions Trial No.197/2019 acquitting the accused persons, namely, Mohammad Tarik (husband of deceased Rimsha),
Mohammad Laeek (father-in-law of deceased Rimsha), Seema (mother-in-law of deceased Rimsha)
and Jainab @ Aman Ali (brother-in-law of deceased Rimsha) from the charges under Sections 498A and 304B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "I.P.C") and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 196, which does not call for any interference.
20 Criminal Appeal No.1774/2020 and M.Cr.C No.33573/2020 fail and are dismissed.
21 Let record of the learned Trial Court be sent back forthwith.
